written: 2026-10-17, by hand from the builder's source, before any run
scoring: Each focus checklist is scored against the concatenation of that focus's documents. The statement is the criterion; accept_any lists phrasings that count as stating it when used about the same thing.
pattern_syntax: evidence.pattern is a JavaScript RegExp source applied with the m flag to the file at evidence.path (relative to the build root); when evidence.path is a directory it is applied to the directory's entry names; evidence.absent true means the pattern must not match.

tech.statement: The service is written in Go; go.mod declares module example.com/linkcheck with the go 1.23 directive.
There are no third-party dependencies: go.mod has no require directive and every import is from the standard library or the module itself.
The listen address comes from the LINKCHECK_ADDR environment variable, default :9090.
The data directory comes from the LINKCHECK_DATA environment variable, default data.
HTTP is served by the standard library net/http ServeMux with Go 1.22 method-and-path patterns; there is no router framework.
Logging uses log/slog with a JSON handler writing to stdout; a -debug flag lowers the level to debug.
Persistence is JSON files on local disk, one <id>.json file per check in the data directory; there is no database.
The only outbound integration is an HTTP GET to each URL a client submits; the service calls no other external API or service.
A Makefile provides build (go build -o bin/linkcheck ./cmd/linkcheck), test (go test ./...) and lint (go vet ./...) targets.
CI is a GitHub Actions workflow that sets up Go from go.mod with actions/setup-go and runs go vet ./... and go test ./... .
The container image comes from a multi-stage Dockerfile: golang:1.23 builds a static binary with CGO_ENABLED=0 and the final stage is gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12, exposing port 9090.

arch.statement: The single binary's entry point is cmd/linkcheck/main.go: it parses flags, loads the config, opens the store, starts the worker pool and runs the HTTP server.
The code is laid out as cmd/linkcheck plus four internal packages: internal/config, internal/api, internal/check and internal/store.
The HTTP API has three routes, registered in internal/api/handler.go: POST /checks, GET /checks/{id} and GET /healthz.
Checks run asynchronously: POST /checks validates the URL, saves a pending check, queues its id and answers 202 Accepted; a worker fetches the URL later and GET /checks/{id} reads the result.
A fixed pool of 4 worker goroutines (const Workers = 4) reads check ids from a buffered channel of capacity 100.
Pool.Submit is a non-blocking send: when the queue is full it returns false and the API answers 503 Service Unavailable.
The check package defines a Store interface (Load, Save) that the pool depends on; store.FileStore implements it, so store imports check and not the reverse.
A check's status is pending, done or failed; a transport error or a response code of 400 or above marks it failed, and the code is recorded.
Check ids are random 16-character hex strings generated with crypto/rand.
Shutdown is graceful: signal.NotifyContext cancels on SIGINT or SIGTERM, the server shuts down with a 10 second timeout, the workers stop on the context and main waits for them.
Dependencies are wired by hand in main (store, then pool, then the API handler) with no global state and no dependency injection framework.

quality.statement: Errors are wrapped with context using fmt.Errorf and %w (for example "read check %s: %w").
Wrapped errors are tested with errors.Is; the API maps fs.ErrNotExist from the store to 404 Not Found.
Logging is structured key-value slog through an injected *slog.Logger (for example Error("load check", "id", id, "err", err)), not the log package or a global logger.
The tests in internal/check are table-driven: a slice of cases, each run with t.Run.
HTTP behaviour is tested against a local httptest.NewServer, not the network.
The store tests use t.TempDir() for an isolated data directory.
Tests use only the standard testing package with t.Fatalf and t.Errorf; there is no assertion or mocking library.
Tests sit beside the code in the same package (package check, package store), and only internal/check and internal/store have tests.
Tests run with go test ./... (make test and CI); go vet ./... is the only linter (make lint), and there is no golangci-lint configuration.
HTTP handlers are methods on a Server struct that holds the dependencies, and every response goes through a writeJSON helper that sets Content-Type application/json.
Input is validated at the HTTP boundary: request bodies are capped with http.MaxBytesReader at 1 MiB and URLs must parse with url.ParseRequestURI as http or https.

concerns.statement: check.Run uses http.Get with the default client, which has no timeout: a slow or hanging URL can hold one of only four workers indefinitely.
The store builds the file path from the id in GET /checks/{id} with filepath.Join and no validation, so an encoded ../ id can read .json files outside the data directory (path traversal).
Workers increment Pool.completed with no mutex or atomic while other workers and the /healthz handler read it: a data race.
FileStore.Save defers f.Close() on a file it has written and ignores the returned error, so a failed final write can go unreported.
internal/api has no tests: the handlers, their status codes and the input validation are untested.
POST /checks has no rate limiting; only a TODO: rate limit comment marks it, so a client can enqueue checks without bound and fill the queue.
The service fetches any http or https URL a client submits, including loopback and internal addresses, with no allow or deny list (server-side request forgery).
Save truncates and rewrites the file in place with os.Create instead of writing a temporary file and renaming it, so a concurrent read or a crash can see a partial or empty file.
